verses.text: Solomon's song, the song above all songs.
Let him kiss me with those lips of his. Your love is sweeter to me than wine.
Your oils smell amazing. Your name is like oil poured out. No wonder the young women love you.
Take me with you. Let's run! The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends: We'll be glad and celebrate you. We'll praise your love more than wine! Beloved: They're right to love you.
I'm dark and lovely, daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like Solomon's curtains.
Don't stare at me because I'm dark. The sun has burned me. My mother's sons got mad at me and put me in charge of their vineyards. I haven't kept my own vineyard.
Tell me, you my soul loves, where do you let your flock graze? Where do you rest them at noon? Why should I have to wander veiled beside the flocks of your friends?
If you don't know, most beautiful of women, follow the sheep tracks. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
My love, you remind me of a horse pulling Pharaoh's chariots.
Those earrings look beautiful against your cheeks, and the strings of jewels look beautiful around your neck.
We'll make you gold earrings with little silver studs.
While the king sat at his table, the scent of my perfume filled the air.
My love is like a little pouch of myrrh resting between my breasts.
My love is like a bunch of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
Look at you, my love. You're beautiful, so beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.
Look at you, my darling. You're beautiful and so lovely, and our couch is green with fresh growth.
The beams of our home are cedar, and the rafters are fir.
I'm a rose from Sharon, a lily from the valleys.
Like a lily growing among thorns, that's what my love is like among the other young women.
Like an apple tree in the middle of the woods, that's what my love is like among the other young men. I loved sitting in his shade. His fruit tasted sweet to me.
He took me into the banquet hall. The banner he raised over me was love.
Give me raisins to get my strength back. Refresh me with apples. I'm weak with love.
His left hand cradles my head, and his right arm wraps around me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the does out in the field. Don't stir up love or wake it before it wants to wake.
That's my love's voice! Look, here he comes, leaping over mountains and bounding over hills.
My love is like a gazelle or a young deer. Look, he's standing behind our wall, peeking in through the windows, looking through the lattice.
My love called to me, “Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.
Look, winter's over. The rain has stopped and gone.
Flowers are popping up all over the ground. It's time to sing, and you can hear the turtledove in our land.
Green figs are ripening on the tree. The vines are blooming and filling the air with their scent. Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.”
My dove, tucked in the cracks of the rock, hiding on the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
Catch those foxes for us, the little ones that tear up the vineyards. Our vines are in bloom.
My love is mine and I'm his. He grazes among the lilies.
Till the day cools down and the shadows slip away, turn, my love, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
At night, there on my bed, I looked for the one my soul loves. I looked, but I couldn't find him.
I'll get up and go around the city. I'll look for the one my soul loves in the streets and the squares. I looked, but I couldn't find him.
The guards making their rounds found me. “Have you seen the one my soul loves?”
I'd barely gone past them when I found the one my soul loves. I held him and wouldn't let go till I'd brought him into my mother's house, to the room of the woman who conceived me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the does out in the field. Don't stir up love or wake it before it wants to wake.
Who's this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense and all the spices a merchant sells?
Look, it's Solomon's carriage! Sixty mighty men surround it, some of Israel's strongest.
Every one of them can handle a sword and knows how to fight. Each has his sword at his side because of the dangers at night.
King Solomon had a carriage made for himself from wood from Lebanon.
He made its posts silver, its base gold, and its seat purple. The daughters of Jerusalem lined the inside with love.
Come out, daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon wearing the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, the day his heart was full of joy.
Look at you, my love. You're beautiful, so beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair flows like a flock of goats coming down Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of freshly shorn sheep coming back from washing. Every one has its twin, with none missing.
Your lips are like scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Behind your veil, your temples look like slices of pomegranate.
Your neck is like David's tower, built to store weapons. A thousand shields hang there, all belonging to mighty warriors.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins born to a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.
Till the day cools down and the shadows slip away, I'll go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
You're beautiful through and through, my love. There's no flaw in you.

Come with me from Lebanon, my bride. Come away from Lebanon with me. Look out from the top of Amana, from the peaks of Senir and Hermon, from where the lions den and the leopards live in the mountains.
You've stolen my heart, my sister, my bride. One glance from you, one chain on your neck, and my heart is yours.
Your love is beautiful, my sister, my bride. It's so much better than wine, and your perfume smells better than all the spices.
Your lips drip like honeycomb, my bride. Honey and milk are under your tongue. Your clothes smell like Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, is a garden locked up tight, a spring shut away, a fountain sealed.
Your new growth is a pomegranate orchard full of prized fruit, with henna and spikenard,
with spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, every kind of incense tree, myrrh and aloes, and all the best spices.
You're a fountain for the gardens, a well of fresh running water, streams flowing down from Lebanon.
Wake up, north wind! Come on, south wind! Blow across my garden so the scent of its spices drifts out. Let my love come into his garden and taste its precious fruit.
I've come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I've gathered my myrrh and spices, eaten my honeycomb and honey, and drunk my wine and milk. Friends: Eat, friends! Drink your fill, you who are loved!
I was asleep, but my heart was awake. That's my love's voice at the door! “Open up for me, my sister, my love, my dove, my flawless one. My head is soaked with dew, my hair wet from the night.”
I've already taken my robe off. Do I really have to put it back on? I've washed my feet. Do I have to get them dirty again?
My love reached in through the opening by the latch, and my heart started pounding for him.
I got up to open the door for him. My hands dripped myrrh. Liquid myrrh ran from my fingers onto the handles of the lock.
I opened the door for my love, but he'd turned and gone. My heart had gone out to him when he spoke. I looked and couldn't find him. I called and got no answer.
The guards making their rounds found me. They beat me and left me bruised. The guards on the walls took my cloak from me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, promise me this. If you find my love, tell him I'm weak with love.
What makes your love better than anyone else's, most beautiful of women? What's so special about him that you're making us promise this?
My love is bright and ruddy. He stands out among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold. His hair is thick and black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside streams, washed with milk and set like jewels.
His cheeks are like beds of spice with mounds of perfume. His lips are like lilies dripping liquid myrrh.
His hands are like gold rings set with beryl. His body is like carved ivory covered with sapphires.
His legs are like marble pillars set on bases of pure gold. He looks like Lebanon, majestic as its cedars.
His mouth is sweetness itself. Everything about him is lovely. This is my love, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
Where did your love go, most beautiful of women? Which way did he turn? We'll help you look for him.
My love has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices. He's gone to graze his flock in the gardens and pick lilies.
I belong to my love, and my love belongs to me. He grazes among the lilies.
You're as beautiful as Tirzah, my love, as lovely as Jerusalem, as awe-inspiring as an army with its banners raised.
Look away for a moment. Your eyes overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats resting along the slopes of Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes coming up from washing. Each has a twin and none is missing.
Your temples look like slices of pomegranate behind your veil.
There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and more young women than you can count.

My dove, my perfect one, is one of a kind. She's her mother's only daughter, the favorite of the woman who bore her. The young women saw her and called her blessed. The queens and concubines saw her and praised her.
Who's this looking out like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, and awe-inspiring as an army with its banners raised?
I went down to the grove of nut trees to see the valley's green shoots, to see whether the vines had budded and the pomegranates had bloomed.
Before I knew what was happening, my desire had put me among the chariots of my royal people.
Come back, come back, Shulammite! Come back, let us look at you! Lover: Why do you want to watch the Shulammite as if you were watching the dance of Mahanaim?
Your feet look beautiful in sandals, daughter of a prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels made by a skilled craftsperson.
Your body is like a round cup that never runs out of mixed wine. Your waist is like a mound of wheat with lilies all around it.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins born to a gazelle.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon looking toward Damascus.
Your head rises like Mount Carmel, and your hair is like purple cloth. A king is held captive by those locks.
You're so beautiful, my love, so lovely and full of delight!
You stand like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
I said, “I'll climb the palm and take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of grapes, and your breath as sweet as apples.
Your mouth is like the finest wine, going down smoothly for my love, slipping past the lips of people who are asleep.
I belong to my love, and he wants me.
Come on, my love. Let's go out into the fields and spend the night in the villages.
Let's get up early and go to the vineyards. We'll see if the vines have budded, if their flowers have opened, and if the pomegranates are blooming. That's where I'll give you my love.
The mandrakes fill the air with their scent. At our doors is every kind of precious fruit, new and old, that I've saved for you, my love.
I wish you were like a brother to me, someone who nursed at my mother's breasts. If I met you outside, I could kiss you and nobody would look down on me.
I'd lead you to my mother's house, where she could teach me. I'd give you spiced wine to drink, juice from my own pomegranate.
His left hand would cradle my head, and his right arm would wrap around me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, promise me this. Don't stir up love or wake it before it wants to wake.
Who's this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her love? Beloved: I woke you under the apple tree. That's where your mother conceived you, where she went into labor and gave birth to you.
Set me like a seal on your heart, like a seal on your arm. Love is strong as death, and jealousy is as cruel as the grave. Its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of the LORD himself.
All the water in the world can't put love out, and floods can't drown it. If someone offered every bit of their family's wealth for love, people would laugh them to scorn.
We have a little sister whose breasts haven't grown yet. What will we do for her when someone comes asking to marry her?
If she's a wall, we'll build a silver turret on her. If she's a door, we'll close her in with cedar boards.
I'm a wall, and my breasts are like towers. That's how I became someone who found peace in his eyes.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He rented it out to caretakers. Each one was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
My own vineyard is mine to decide about. You can have the thousand, Solomon, and two hundred go to the people who tend the fruit.
You who live in the gardens, with friends listening in, let me hear your voice!
Come away, my love! Be like a gazelle or a young stag out on the mountains of spices!
